data.headline: Raise price 3% and boost marketing 20%
data.why: The plan lifts margin and uses marketing to keep the 60% who already prefer you. News shows wheat costs are falling, so the 3% rise adds cushion without matching the rival's $5.50. Cash on hand covers the marketing spend.
data.watch_out: Egg prices may jump over 40% this year, eating the extra margin. If cost surge hits before marketing pulls new volume, cash could tighten.
data.recheck_when: Watch next USDA wheat report or egg-price spike; re-evaluate by week 8.

series.label: US hard red winter wheat price

realized_case.label: What happened: Flour −1%
realized_case.why: What the input's price really did next
realized_case.cost_line: Flour −1% by October (−2% at the peak in August) × 33% of your cost is flour = your cost 0% (−$0.01 a loaf)

what_happened.text: The World Bank's monthly price for US hard red winter wheat stayed between $231 and $246 a tonne from May to November 2025, against $237 in May.

caveats: Flour is about a third of a loaf's cost in the owner's own words. Flour prices follow wheat with milling and freight on top, so they move less than wheat in percent.
The series is US hard red winter wheat (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/mt), the usual bread wheat. It is a 'nothing happened' case: the news in spring 2025 was about tariffs, but wheat stayed flat.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.
